classification.difficultyReason: Exponentiate logarithmic equations, solve the resulting linear or quadratic equations, and reject roots outside the logarithmic domain.

content.prompt: Solve these equations by making both sides indices of powers with the same base. Check your solutions to make sure that LHS and RHS are defined when they are substituted.

answer.worked:
The logarithms require $-1<x<11$.

$$\begin{align*}2^{\log_2(x+1)}&=2^{\log_2(11-x)+1}\\x+1&=2(11-x)\\x+1&=22-2x\\3x&=21\\x&=7\end{align*}$$

At $x=7$, the logarithm arguments are $8$ and $4$, both positive. Also, $\log_2 8=3$ and $\log_2 4+1=3$, so the solution is valid.

All logarithm arguments must be positive, requiring $x>3$.

$$\begin{align*}3^{\log_3(x+3)+\log_3(x-3)}&=3^{\log_3(4x+3)}\\(x+3)(x-3)&=4x+3\\x^2-9&=4x+3\\x^2-4x-12&=0\\(x-6)(x+2)&=0\\x&=6\text{ or }-2\end{align*}$$

Reject $x=-2$, which is outside $x>3$. At $x=6$, the arguments are $9$, $3$ and $27$, all positive, and $\log_3 9+\log_3 3=2+1=3=\log_3 27$. Hence $x=6$.

answer.short:
$x=8$.

Reject $x=-1$ because the original logarithms are not all defined.
answer.worked:
All logarithm arguments must be positive, requiring $x>3$.

$$\begin{align*}2^{\log_2 x+\log_2(x-3)-\log_2(x+2)}&=2^2\\\frac{x(x-3)}{x+2}&=4\\x(x-3)&=4(x+2)\\x^2-3x&=4x+8\\x^2-7x-8&=0\\(x-8)(x+1)&=0\\x&=8\text{ or }-1\end{align*}$$

Reject $x=-1$, which is outside $x>3$. At $x=8$, the arguments are $8$, $5$ and $10$, all positive. The LHS is $\log_2(8\times\frac{5}{10})=\log_2 4=2$, so $x=8$ is valid.
